subject: physics_2
question_text: Explain the principle and working of a nuclear reactor with the help of a labelled diagram.

verification.note: The 1+2+1+1+1+2 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. The 1+2+1+1+1+2 split is INVENTED; the 2 marks on the diagram follow the words "with the help of a labelled diagram" in the question. The book prints "labeled"; the spelling is normalised here. Hand-checked against the book's own five-part list (fuel, moderator, control rods, radiation shielding, coolant). The diagram is drawn with five labelled parts only: the renderer draws outlines with no fills, so a part cannot be hidden inside another, and every label needs its own clear lane.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Principle
steps.mark_note: Controlled chain reaction in enriched uranium
lines: Principle: a nuclear reactor works on the
principle of a controlled chain reaction in
natural uranium U-238 enriched with U-235.
The heat generated is used to produce
electricity.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words "controlled chain reaction" carry it.
steps.why: A reactor and a bomb use the same nuclear reaction; the whole difference is that a reactor holds the multiplication factor at K = 1.
common_mistakes: Saying a reactor works on fusion. It works on fission.

recall.must_convey: That a nuclear reactor works on the principle of a controlled chain reaction in uranium enriched with U-235, generating heat.
accept: uranium two thirty eight enriched with uranium two thirty five
reject: fuel moderator control rods shielding coolant

steps.memory_tip: Same reaction as the bomb, held at K = 1.

steps.label: Labelled diagram
steps.mark_note: Core with fuel rods, control rod, moderator, coolant, shielding
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The examiner looks for the core with fuel rods, a control rod entering from above, the moderator, the coolant path and the shielding.
steps.why: The picture makes the three separate jobs visible at once: the fuel rods make the neutrons, the moderator between them slows the neutrons, and the control rod removes neutrons from above.
common_mistakes: Drawing the control rod outside the core. It must reach into the core.
Labelling the moderator as the coolant. The moderator fills the space between the fuel rods.

recall.must_convey: That the reactor is drawn with a shielded core holding fuel rods, a control rod entering from above, the moderator between the rods, and the coolant path.
accept: draw the core with fuel rods and a control rod
label the moderator shielding and coolant
reject: heavy water and graphite slow the neutrons

steps.memory_tip: Draw the box, then the rods inside, then the rod coming down from the top.

steps.label: Fuel and moderator
steps.mark_note: U-235 fuel rods; heavy water or graphite moderator
lines: 1. Fuel: the fuel is made into thin, long
cylindrical rods of uranium enriched in U-235.
The part of the reactor holding the fuel is
called the core.
2. Moderator: heavy water or graphite is placed
between the fuel rods to slow the fast
neutrons down to thermal neutrons.
steps.margin_note: The fuel and the moderator share one mark. Name a material for each.
steps.why: Enrichment matters because natural uranium is over 99% U-238, which does not undergo fission with thermal neutrons.
common_mistakes: Naming cadmium as the moderator. Cadmium absorbs neutrons and is a control rod.
Saying the fuel is U-238. The fissile part is U-235.

recall.must_convey: That the fuel is uranium enriched in U-235 in the form of rods in the core, and the moderator is heavy water or graphite that slows the fast neutrons.
accept: heavy water or graphite as moderator

steps.memory_tip: Fuel makes neutrons, moderator slows them — two parts, one mark.

steps.label: Control rods
steps.mark_note: Cadmium or boron rods absorb neutrons
lines: 3. Control rods: cadmium or boron rods are
lowered into the core to absorb neutrons.
Their depth sets how many neutrons are left
to continue the chain reaction, so the
multiplication factor is held at K = 1.
steps.margin_note: One mark. Name the material AND the purpose.
steps.why: The control rods are the only quick adjustment the reactor has, so they are what makes the difference between a steady output and a runaway one.
common_mistakes: Saying the control rods slow the neutrons. They absorb them.
Naming graphite. Graphite is the moderator.

recall.must_convey: That control rods of cadmium or boron are lowered into the core to absorb neutrons and hold the multiplication factor at 1.

steps.label: Shielding and coolant
steps.mark_note: Concrete or lead shield; water or molten sodium coolant
lines: 4. Shielding: β and γ rays given out during
fission are harmful, so the reactor is
surrounded by a thick concrete, steel or lead
shield that absorbs them.
5. Coolant: water or molten sodium is circulated
to carry the heat away from the fuel rods.
steps.margin_note: One mark for both. Name a material for each.
steps.why: The coolant does two jobs at once: it keeps the fuel rods from overheating and it carries the useful heat out to the boiler.
common_mistakes: Saying the shield stops neutrons only. It absorbs the β and γ radiation.
Leaving the coolant out. Without it there is no way to use the heat.

recall.must_convey: That a thick concrete, steel or lead shield absorbs the harmful beta and gamma rays, and a coolant such as water or molten sodium carries the heat away.
accept: concrete shield absorbs beta and gamma
coolant is water or molten sodium
removes the heat from the fuel

steps.memory_tip: Shield keeps radiation in; coolant takes heat out.

steps.label: Working
steps.mark_note: Fission to thermal neutrons to steam to generator
lines: Working: the uranium fuel rods sit in the core
with the graphite moderator between them.
A few U-235 nuclei undergo fission and release
fast neutrons. These pass through the
moderator, lose energy and become thermal
neutrons, which are captured by U-235 and
carry the chain reaction on.
The control rods hold the reaction steady.
The heat produced turns water into steam, the
steam drives a turbine, and the turbine drives
a generator that produces electricity.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Follow one chain from the first fission to the electricity.
steps.why: Only the first link is nuclear; from the steam onwards a nuclear power station is an ordinary thermal power station.
common_mistakes: Saying electricity is produced directly by fission. The heat drives a steam turbine.
Leaving out the moderator step. The fast neutrons must be slowed before they are captured.

recall.must_convey: That fission neutrons are slowed by the moderator, captured by U-235 to continue the chain reaction under the control rods, and the heat produced makes steam that drives a turbine and a generator.
accept: fast neutrons are slowed by the moderator

steps.memory_tip: Nuclear only as far as the heat; after that it is an ordinary steam plant.

insider_note: Eight marks, and the five named parts carry three of them. Write the list with a one-line job for each part rather than a paragraph.
